::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
Intel's remaining manufacturing presence in China, after fully divesting its only China wafer fab (the Dalian NAND plant) to SK Hynix. Chengdu is an assembly-and-test (ATP) site, not a fab — it packages and tests chips rather than fabricating wafers. Intel had invested $600 million in the site by December 2014, when it announced a further $1.6 billion over 15 years; in 2024 it added $300 million in registered capital to expand server-chip packaging and test.
:::

**Chinese name:** 英特尔产品（成都）有限公司 (Yīngtè'ěr Chǎnpǐn (Chéngdū) Yǒuxiàn Gōngsī)

## What does this facility make?

Chip assembly and test services for Intel products — the step between finished wafers and sellable packaged chips, not wafer fabrication.

## Why does it matter?

With Dalian fully transferred to SK Hynix, Chengdu's ATP operation is the clearest marker of what 'Intel in China' now means: assembly and test only, no fab. Included here to avoid the common misconception (prompted by Intel's historical Dalian fab) that Intel still operates a wafer fab in China.

## Packaging Technology Trajectory

- **2005**: Assembly & test (client CPUs) begins operation
- **2016**: Intel Advanced Test Technology in mass production (planned H2 2016)
- **2024**: Server-chip packaging & test added (announced; US$300M capital increase)
- **2026**: Wafer pre-processing + advanced packaging + test (stated, as of)

## Project Timeline

- **Sep 2026** — Becomes Intel's sole remaining manufacturing site in China once the Dalian fab's transfer to SK Hynix is finalized
